terms.comment: Traupman’s term: verbum inaequāle, an irregular verb (volō, nōlō, fīō), and inaequāliter dēclīnātur, it is declined irregularly (247). The word is classical in the senses “uneven, unequal” (Ovid, Quintilian); Lewis & Short gives no grammatical sense. Varro’s word for irregularity in grammar is anōmalia (LL 9.3, Lewis & Short), set against analogia, regularity.

phrases.latin: Quārē inaequālia dīcuntur? — Quia dēclīnātiōnēs extrā rēgulam sunt.
phrases.english: Why are they called irregular? — Because they are conjugated outside the pattern.
an irregular verb (like volō, I want)
